title: Solve Subject–Verb Agreement with the Odd-One-Out Trick
description: Use he and they to classify complete verb phrases, treat a three-to-one split as a clue, and confirm the answer with the sentence’s actual subject and time relationships.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Under the current rules, the box of spare keys ______ in a locked drawer.
questions.explanation_html: The subject is the singular box. “Of spare keys” modifies it. The box belongs.
questions.variation: Read the true subject through an intervening phrase

distractor_notes.A: Agrees with the nearby plural keys.
distractor_notes.C: Uses a plural helper and an unsuitable form.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Several recordings that the archive received last month ______ currently being restored.
questions.explanation_html: Several recordings is plural, and “currently” calls for the ongoing present action. “Are being restored” is the full verb phrase.
questions.variation: Classify the full verb phrase using its helping verb

distractor_notes.D: Does not form a complete progressive construction here.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Last night, after the audience went home, the stage crew ______ all the equipment into storage.
questions.explanation_html: The crew completed the action last night. “Moved” is a complete past-tense verb.
questions.variation: Use the time clue when agreement alone cannot settle the choice

distractor_notes.C: Places the event in the future.
distractor_notes.D: Leaves the sentence without a finite verb.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: During the restoration, the stone steps near the gate ______ unsafe for visitors until builders replaced them.
questions.explanation_html: The steps are plural, and the restoration is a completed past period. Choose the plural past form “were.”
questions.variation: Resolve agreement in past forms and when no answer-count shortcut works

distractor_notes.A: Agrees with singular gate rather than plural steps.
distractor_notes.C: Uses singular agreement and present tense.
distractor_notes.D: Uses present tense for a finished past period.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The workers ______ the old coating when a second crew arrived to help them finish.
questions.explanation_html: The plural workers were already engaged in an action that was still ongoing when the second crew arrived.
questions.variation: Use an ongoing past action to frame a later event

distractor_notes.D: Places the work after the past event.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The set of pumps installed near the southern ramps ______ only one room at a time when it operates.
questions.explanation_html: The set is a singular subject, and the sentence describes what it does under normal operation. “Serves” supplies the matching verb.
questions.variation: Read the true subject through an intervening phrase

distractor_notes.A: Agrees with the plural noun pumps.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Since the new sign was installed, the visitor count ______ steadily increasing.
questions.explanation_html: The subject count is singular. “Since” gives the time span, and “has been increasing” expresses the continuing change.
questions.variation: Classify the full verb phrase using its helping verb

distractor_notes.A: Agrees with plural visitors rather than singular count.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Next month, before the new tanks arrive, the technicians ______ the rooms for the first time.
questions.explanation_html: The preparation is planned for a future time and has not happened yet. “Will prepare” fits that timing.
questions.variation: Use the time clue when agreement alone cannot settle the choice

distractor_notes.A: Places the first event in the past.
distractor_notes.B: Uses singular agreement and the wrong time.
distractor_notes.D: Leaves the sentence without a complete verb.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: At last night’s preview, the row of spotlights ______ too bright until the crew dimmed it.
questions.explanation_html: The row is the singular subject. The event took place last night, so the sentence requires “was.”
questions.variation: Resolve agreement in past forms and when no answer-count shortcut works

distractor_notes.D: Uses plural agreement and present tense.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The sculptor ______ a fresh mold when the power went out, interrupting her work.
questions.explanation_html: The sculptor is singular. The outage interrupted an action already underway, which calls for “was preparing.”
questions.variation: Use an ongoing past action to frame a later event

distractor_notes.C: Treats the preparation as completed and uses the wrong time frame.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The sleeves of the protective jacket ______ heat from reaching the wearer’s arms.
questions.explanation_html: The sleeves are the plural subject. The singular jacket belongs to an intervening prepositional phrase.
questions.variation: Read the true subject through an intervening phrase

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: Today, the devices in the cabinet ______ already stopped transmitting.
questions.explanation_html: The devices are plural. “Have stopped” is the complete verb phrase that agrees and fits the completed event.
questions.variation: Classify the full verb phrase using its helping verb

distractor_notes.C: Cannot complete the perfect form and is singular.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The fans ______ in 1987, the same year the hall opened, and were removed decades later.
questions.explanation_html: The fans are plural and received the action in a specified past year. “Were installed” fits both constraints.
questions.variation: Use the time clue when agreement alone cannot settle the choice

distractor_notes.A: Places the installation in the present.
distractor_notes.D: Makes the fans the actors and uses the wrong time.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: When the survey ended last year, the balance of the funds ______ still available, so the director transferred it that day.
questions.explanation_html: The pronoun “it” also points to the singular balance. It was available in a specified past period.
questions.variation: Resolve agreement in past forms and when no answer-count shortcut works

distractor_notes.D: Uses present tense and plural agreement.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The crews responsible for the north wing ______ replacement panels in the rain when a loose cable brought the installation to a temporary stop.
questions.explanation_html: The plural crews were in the middle of positioning the panels when the interruption occurred.
questions.variation: Use an ongoing past action to frame a later event

distractor_notes.C: Does not fit the unfinished action interrupted by the cable.
distractor_notes.D: Places the action after the already stated interruption.
